request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold.
Holding writes PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action
(a hold ends on its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold.
Holding writes PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action
(a hold ends on its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates, a person can have several of them, and `bin/e2e` passes.

**How it works now**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V24__person_hold_interval.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table holding a from-date and an optional to-date. Anyone already on hold carries over as one hold with no from-date (from the beginning of time) and no end. The old `held` column is dropped.
- **Server:** `POST …/people/{id}/hold` now takes `{from, to}` and always adds a new hold. An empty from-date means the sheet's today; an empty to-date means the hold has no end. It refuses a date that isn't a real date, or a to-date earlier than the from-date. The audit line is `PERSON_HELD … name=<name> from=<date>`.
- **Totals:** only a person's live claims dated within one of their holds are left out. Their settled claims and their claims outside any hold still count. This applies to the on-screen totals and to the due-total fixed when a period is closed.
- **Screen:** "On hold" shows yes/no for whether the person has any hold at all. Below it, each hold is listed as its own line, followed by from and to date fields and a Hold button. The Release button and the `PERSON_RELEASED` audit record are gone.

**Choices I made where the request was open:**
- The request says only OPEN claims are left out. I also left out PENDING claims, because the app treats those as open in every total and the old hold did the same.
- Hold dates count as inclusive at both ends.
- The test doesn't cover the refusal for a to-date earlier than the from-date. That case is rejected both on screen and by the server.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing. The rules live in about 195 small Java step classes, wired together by YAML files under `rest/api/`, plus a React front end that works out most of the figures itself. Paths below are relative to `src/main/java/.../hq/app` and `src/main/frontend/features`. ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Per claim (`claims/claims.slot.tsx`, `ClaimResponse`) | testid | What it shows / rule | |---|---| | `claim-amount` | The amount with two decimals. A negative amount makes the claim a **correction** (`Claim.isCorrection`). A correction must name, in `corrects`, a **SETTLED claim of the same person** by its sheet-wide `number` (`ValidateClaim`, `CheckClaimCorrects`; the client checks with `correctionError`). A non-negative amount must name nothing. Quick-add only accepts amounts of 0.00 or more. | | `claim-date` | A claim given no date takes the **sheet's `today`** (`ApplyClaim`). The real clock is never used. | | `claim-due-by` (`dueBy`) | **Frozen when the claim is created**: its date plus `settings.terms(sheet, grade)`. The grade is the person's grade in force on the claim date (`gradeOn`). The terms are the grade's own `terms-`, else the sheet's `terms`, else 14. Later edits to the date or the terms, and reassigning the claim, don't change it. | | `claim-overdue` | `useOverdue`: the claim is **live** (OPEN or PENDING) and `dueBy < today`. | | `claim-due` | A SETTLED claim shows its frozen `settledDue`. Any other claim's due is computed live (`claimDueCents` on the client, `ClaimDue.now` on the server):
• **Rate:** `findInForce`/`rateOn` gives the rate for the grade in force on the claim date, using the latest rate `from` on or before that date. If there is none, the due is **n/a**.
• **Base:** amount × rate / 100, to 2 decimals.
• **Rounding** (`settings.rounding` / `useRoundsHalfUp`): half up if the claim is dated before `policy-date`, half to even otherwise. When no policy date is set, today is used instead, so rounding can change as today moves.
• **Floor:** the result is raised to at least `floor` (default 1.00).
• **Late charge:** for every full 30 days past `dueBy`, add `late-pct` (default 0) of the floored due, rounded the same way.
• **Corrections** get no floor and no late charge. | | `claim-status` | `ClaimStatus`: DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED, DRAFT/OPEN → VOID, OPEN → PENDING (a clerk's settle), PENDING → SETTLED (approve) or OPEN (reject). SETTLED and VOID are final (`canBecome`, `ClaimTransition`). The client mirrors this in `ALLOWED` / `canTake`. | | `claim-number` | Given on **open** and kept when voided (`ClaimNumbering`). Normally it is the next sheet-wide `number`. When the sheet's today is on or after `period-numbering-from`, it is a `periodNumber` instead: `-`, or `X-` for a claim dated in no period. The shown value is `periodNumber ?? number`. | | `claim-opened-by` | Who opened it (X-User). It drives the four-eyes rule. | | `claim-period` | The period whose from–to range (inclusive) contains the claim date. | | `claim-log` / `ClaimLogEntry` | Written by `ClaimLog.record` whenever the status changes, including the first DRAFT. Each line holds the status, who, today, and the due as `ClaimDue.now` worked it out at that moment. Lines are frozen once written. | ### Per person - **`person-grade`**: the grade in force on today (`PersonResponse.from` → `gradeOn(today)`). Grades are dated (`recordGrade`): - A person's first grade applies from the beginning of time. - Later grades apply from `gradeFrom`, defaulting to today, and replace any grade recorded for the same date. - Recording the grade already in force does nothing. - **`person-claimed`**: `total(claims, useCounts)`, the sum of the **amounts** (corrections included) of the person's claims that count. - **What counts** (`ClaimStatus.counts`, client `counts` / `useCounts`): OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. DRAFT and VOID never count. On top of that, a **live claim dated within one of the person's holds counts in no live total**; their SETTLED claims, and claims outside a hold, still count. - **`person-due-total`** (`useDueTotal`, in `rates/rates.slot.tsx`): the sum of the counting claims' dues, with n/a counted as 0. It shows **n/a** when the person's grade has no rate today and no claim "keeps a figure". A claim keeps a figure if it is settled with a due, or dated under a different grade from today's and has a due. - **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`**: the person's counting, live, overdue claims, and their dues added up. - **`person-hold`**: `held` is "yes" if the person has **any** hold, even one that has expired or not yet started. A hold runs from `from` (default today) to `to` (open-ended if empty), both inclusive. A `to` before `from` is refused. - **`person-retired` / `person-retired-from`**: `retiredFrom` defaults to today, and retiring someone already retired is refused. - A claim dated **after** `retiredFrom` is refused when it is added or edited (`CheckClaimRetired`), quick-added (against today), or reassigned to that person. - Retired people are hidden from the list unless `showRetired` is on or they still have a DRAFT claim. - **`person-patrons` / `person-backing`**: backing is the sum of the patrons' due-totals, skipping n/a. A person can't be their own patron, and the same patron can't be named twice. ### Sheet-wide figures - **`rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-*`**: everyone's figures added up, retired people included. - **`summary-grade-X-count` / `-due-total`**: people **not retired**, grouped by the grade shown for them (today's grade). - **`summary-status-X-count`**: every claim, regardless of whether it counts. - **`period-due-total` / `summary-period-…`** (`usePeriodDue`): - While a period is open, it is the live due of the counting claims dated in it, late charge included. - Once **closed**, it shows the frozen `closedTotal`, which `ClosePeriod` computes on the server. ### What gets frozen, and when | Value | Frozen when | |---|---| | `dueBy` | The claim is created | | `number` / `periodNumber` | The claim is opened | | `settledDue` | The claim is settled or approved; a claim that waited in PENDING keeps building late charge until approval | | Log-line dues | Each status change | | `closedTotal` | The period is closed; reopening makes the total live again | Until a claim is settled, its due moves with any change to rates, floor, late percent, policy date, today or the person's grades. ### A closed period No claim dated inside it can be added, edited (the old date and the new date are both checked), opened, bulk-opened, settled, voided, approved, rejected or reassigned (`CheckClaimPeriod`, `CheckQuickClaimPeriod`). Periods can't overlap, and a period name must be unique on the sheet. ### Who may do what - A role is `clerk` or `steward`. Any name without a role is a clerk (`roleOf`). - **Four eyes:** whoever opened a claim can't settle or approve it (`SelfSettleException`). - **Clerk limit:** when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit`, it goes to **PENDING** instead. With no limit set, or a due of n/a, the claim settles normally. A steward can settle anything. - **Steward only:** approve, reject (which needs a reason), reassign, and reopen a period. - **Reassign:** only DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claims, never a correction, and only to another person on the sheet who isn't retired before the claim date. The claim keeps its number, date and `dueBy`. - **No role check at all:** setting roles (so anyone can make themselves a steward), rates and settings, and adding or closing periods. - **Edits:** only a DRAFT claim can be edited, checked against the stored status (`CheckClaimEditable`). A person edit carrying a stale `version` is refused, and person names must be unique ignoring case. ### Import and quick-add - **Import** (`CheckImport`): each line is `name,grade`, with grade A, B or C and no name repeated in the paste. One bad line refuses the whole import. A name already on the sheet gets the new grade recorded from today; a new name gets a person whose grade applies from the beginning of time. - **Quick-add:** finds the person by name, ignoring case, or creates them with grade A. The claim takes today's date and an empty note. - **Bulk open:** opens the selected DRAFT claims that aren't in a closed period, in person-id then claim-id order. Everything else is counted as refused. ### Inconsistencies I noticed - **Closing a period changes its total.** `ClosePeriod` works out the due without the **late charge**, while the open period's on-screen total includes it. So a period's total can drop the moment it is closed. - **Corrections can't target period-numbered claims.** `CheckClaimCorrects` and `correctionError` look claims up by the sheet-wide `number`, which those claims don't have. - **Due-by goes stale.** Editing a claim's date, or reassigning the claim, leaves `dueBy` based on the old date or the old person's grade. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered. The live-due formula is written three times: `ClaimDue.java`, `claimDueCents` in `rates.ts`, and inline in `ClosePeriod.java`, and those copies already disagree. The "counts / held / live" rule, the status rules and the permission checks are each repeated on the client and the server. The order in which checks run lives only in the YAML pipelines. The comments are good and accurate, but a new developer would have to piece the rules together across dozens of one-method classes and several front-end hooks.
